# Pulse task #2682: W11: Implement reusable nested Audio, MIDI, Instrument and Drum racks

Operation: 9ab1480e465ab8cf03cdf929f8fb5a32
Assignee: PORTALSURFER (Pulse #1, GitHub ID 41680373)

Part of Hex native device roadmap #2661, goal 3, version 0.1. Astra assessment: 17 October 2026.

Goal: all four Live rack families become native graph composition using ordinary devices.

Deliverables:
- Canonical stable-ID nested chain graph with bounded depth/chain/device counts, serial/parallel processing, chain gain/mute/solo, key/velocity/selector zones and crossfades. Retain exact child/automation identity through reorder/group/ungroup/duplicate and Undo.
- Macro mappings with ranges/inversion/normalization, one-to-many edits, nested targets, variations/snapshots and atomic state/preset changes. Shared parameter precedence comes from W05.
- Instrument racks admit multiple instrument branches; MIDI racks preserve generated event ownership; audio racks sum compensated outputs; drum racks provide pads/note mapping/chokes/returns/outputs and chain extraction using these same primitives.
- Generalize the current single freely positioned instrument rule only inside explicitly typed compiled graph semantics. Do not bolt extra instruments into an ad hoc UI-only list.
- Reuse bounded tail/history/admission rules for nested removal/replacement, bypass and stopped topology changes; asset-aware rack presets use W10.

Acceptance: all four rack types save/reopen, Undo, automate/macromap and render identically through Arrangement/Session/export. Independent parallel-chain/zone/choke/multioutput/latency tests cover order and crossfades. Cycles/depth/resource overflow refuse atomically; child removal leaves no dangling automation or notes. Native pad/chain editing uses W07 with keyboard alternatives.

Sources: current hex-project/device.rs ordered chain; engine routing/latency; lattice lifecycle; official rack reference. This is a new graph capability, not completion of #16's finite original chain scope.

Planning workstream: split implementation into focused PRs as work begins. Related canonical tickets: #16, #28, #2375. Preserve their current scope, versions, status and PR history. Dependency edges order the enabling contracts; downstream production proof is qualified incrementally under W20.

Execution order: blocked by #2674, #2676, #2677, #2680, #2681. Complete the recorded prerequisite contracts before starting this workstream. When all prerequisites are satisfied, return this issue to todo. Independent workstreams may proceed in parallel once their own blockers are cleared.

17 October 2026 user product decision — Instrument Grid
The pad grouping device is named Instrument Grid (native app label `instrument grid`), superseding Pad Grid/Device Grid proposals. Include it explicitly in the native device list and this rack workstream. Ableton Drum Rack and Bitwig Drum Machine remain reference terminology, not a restriction to drums.

Both sample-file drops and full instrument-device drops onto pads must work. A sample drop creates an ordinary sample-device child using W10 asset leases/W15 sample voices; an instrument drop admits the complete instrument device/state as a normal child, preserving authored identity/mappings/preset semantics according to explicit copy-versus-move rules. Define occupied-pad replacement, invalid/unsupported drops, multi-file ordering, loading/cancellation and resource refusal before implementation; refuse atomically without losing the previous pad or project data. Do not implement a separate sample-only bank. Preserve all existing nested rack identity, MIDI ownership, choke/return/multioutput, latency, lifetime, save/reopen/Undo and graph-bound acceptance above.

Acceptance additionally requires real sample and full instrument drops, persistence/reopen and one-Undo edits, safe rejection/cancellation/replacement, note ownership and rendered Arrangement/Session/export behavior. Provide keyboard alternatives through W07. Naming/drop planning does not start implementation or change prerequisite order.
